lines.text: From pearl divers and copper traders to a union of seven emirates and the tallest tower on Earth. This is the story of the United Arab Emirates.
For thousands of years, the people of this coast dived for pearls. It was the Gulf's great trade until cultured pearls, and then oil.
Over four thousand years ago this was Magan, a land of copper miners whose metal was traded all the way to Sumer.
In the seventeen hundreds a settlement grew on the island of Abu Dhabi, one day to be the capital and the richest of the emirates.
From 1820 treaties with Britain ended the raids at sea and bound the sheikhdoms of the coast to Britain, as the Trucial States.
In 1833 Dubai began as a small pearling and trading town by its creek, the seed of a global city.
Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, born in 1918, would rule Abu Dhabi, found the union and become its first president.
Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum would become ruler of Dubai and the union's prime minister, and drive the city's rise.
Then, in 1958, oil was found off Abu Dhabi. The first cargo sailed four years later, and everything began to change.
Mohamed bin Zayed, born in 1961, would follow his father as ruler of Abu Dhabi, and become president of the union in 2022.
In 1971 Abu Dhabi founded its national oil company, ADNOC, to run the wealth beneath its sands and seas.
That same year, as Britain withdrew, six emirates united under Sheikh Zayed, and Ras al-Khaimah joined soon after. The UAE was born.
In 1985 Dubai launched its own airline, Emirates, and made the city a crossroads between the continents.
In 1999 the Burj Al Arab opened, a hotel shaped like a sail, standing on its own island.
Two years later work began on Palm Jumeirah, an island built out into the sea in the shape of a palm tree.
Abu Dhabi turned to art. The Louvre Abu Dhabi, under a great dome of latticed steel, opened its doors in 2017.
In 2007 the vast white Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque opened, named for the founder who is buried beside it.
And in 2010 came the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, more than eight hundred metres high, the tallest building in the world.
In 2020 the Emirates sent the Hope probe to Mars, the first Arab mission to another planet. It reached orbit the next year.
That same year the UAE signed the Abraham Accords, opening ties with Israel.
And in 2021 Dubai hosted the world's fair, Expo 2020, welcoming millions of visitors.
From the pearl coast to the edge of space, the story of the Emirates has only just begun.
